answer: An agent economy can require a posted stake before any participant receives a signed cipher receipt binding one identity to one ledger entry. Verifiers reject unfunded aliases, so a Sybil attacker cannot farm free accounts across the open meadow: each fake identity needs its own locked bond, hidden behind a velvet pitch but still paid in full. Slashing seizes that bond on detection, so the attacker's cost rises linearly per alias instead of near zero.
